messages:
sophia: Customer hitting partial SSE output after reconnect. They see Python iterator raise RuntimeError("resume mid-token") and the TS client drops the final closing JSON chunk. Reported after ~3 reconnect attempts in 30s window.

mike: Can you paste the repro steps/customer timeline?

sophia: Sure — customer flow:
1) open SSE to /v1/stream (model A)
2) auth token rotates (they use short-lived token) -> client reconnects quickly
3) our routing picks fallback node w/ model variant B (hand-off) -> stream resumes but outputs are garbled/partial
4) python iterator raises, TS client ends with truncated JSON.

mike: Any logs? request ids?

sophia: Attached minimal logs from their session (sanitized):
```
INFO 2024-05-12T18:02:41Z session=svc-92 connect token_id=tok-123 start_stream
WARN 2024-05-12T18:02:55Z session=svc-92 auth=rotate token_id=tok-124 reconnect
DEBUG 2024-05-12T18:02:55Z session=svc-92 route=hand_off target=node-fallback reason=auth-rotate
ERROR 2024-05-12T18:02:55Z session=svc-92 resume_error kv_uuid_mismatch prev_kv=kv-77 new_kv=kv-88
WARN 2024-05-12T18:02:55Z session=svc-92 stream_partial last_frame="}" expected="]]"
```

elaine: kv_uuid_mismatch stands out. That suggests the resumed worker didn't have the right KV cache for the model/token. If we resume on a node with different kv state the tokenization/offsets can be off -> partial tokens and iterator failures.

daniel: Repro locally? mike: I tried a quick repro using curl to simulate rotating tokens and two concurrent connects. Repro steps:
```
# open initial sse
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer TEMP1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-6b","stream":true}' \
  &
# rotate token in test harness then reconnect immediately
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer TEMP2" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-6b","stream":true}'
```
I see same kv_uuid_mismatch and the python async iterator throws: RuntimeError: resume mid-token

mike: Interesting — our resume currently matches on token value and sequence id. If token rotates mid-handoff we might be looking up cache by the old token id and failing.

elaine: Quick mitigation: we should prefer session_id (persistent across token refresh) for cache lookup during resume, and only validate token for auth not KV mapping. Also increase a grace window so transient reconnects route back to same worker if possible.

devx-bot: @mike assigned issue #INF-9210 (sse: resume by session_id + grace window). Canary planned.

daniel: Small additional detail — TS client code uses EventSource polyfill which drops final chunk if it doesn't end with delimiter "\n\n". Combined with truncated frame we end up with incomplete JSON parse on client. Workaround for users: add retry logic that buffers until matching brackets or re-request the tail via non-streaming API.

mike: Proposed PR:
- change resume key: lookup by session_id first, fallback to token-based for legacy
- update handshake to include session_version and kv_uuid assertion; if mismatch return a 409 with hint rather than attempting blind resume
- add server-side grace window 5s during token rotate to keep session pinned to worker if reconnect within window

elaine: Sounds good. Add integration test that rotates token during inflight stream and asserts no RuntimeError and that final JSON is complete.

sophia: Customer patch notes & workaround?

mike: Patch merged to main, will backport to 1.x. Canary deploy in 20m. Workaround for customer: set "session_pin":true in SDK config (available in our next patch) or temporarily increase token TTL. I pinged them.

ops-bot: Canary deployment for INF-9210 started (canary group: 12% traffic).

sophia: Thanks — I'll update the support ticket and ask them to verify after canary. If they still see issues we'll grab a live session with debug logs. :thumbsup:
